card.name: Yosakoi
card.tagline: Modern high-energy team dance with naruko clappers
card.profile: Yosakoi is a dynamic style of Japanese group dance that originated in Kochi Prefecture in 1954, when the city held the first Yosakoi Matsuri to revitalize the local economy after the war (Wikipedia). It combines traditional Japanese dance movement with modern music and is performed by large costumed teams (Wikipedia). Dancers must hold naruko - small wooden clappers historically used by farmers to scare birds - and must dance while moving forward, while the music must include part of Eisaku Takemasa's 'Yosakoi Naruko Odori' song (Wikipedia). Takemasa released the copyright to the public, encouraging adaptation (Grokipedia). The style spread nationwide, notably to Sapporo's Yosakoi Soran Festival (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Sapporo's Yosakoi Soran Festival, per Hokkaido's official Domingo tourism site, 'began with 10 teams and 1,000 participants in 1992' and today 'sees around 30,000 participants from Japan and overseas, and attracts around 2 million spectators' (Domingo, Hokkaido).
